assets/vo/s01-dce830e0.mp3: Why did Anthropic stop using git, and what did they build instead?
assets/vo/s02-a7d3f347.mp3: In May, they merged 2,500 code changes a day.
assets/vo/s02-2d56ffa2.mp3: The bottleneck became tools built for humans, like git.
assets/vo/s03-2ab0e002.mp3: Git gives every copy the whole project and its entire history.
assets/vo/s03-7c95bc02.mp3: So you can work offline. For most projects, that's perfect.
assets/vo/s04-425f0e93.mp3: But all of Anthropic's code lives in one giant project, with almost 100 gigabytes of history.
assets/vo/s04-23e7bd17.mp3: Each copy is over 25 gigabytes, and test jobs check out code 25 million times a day.
assets/vo/s05-f3a3d57b.mp3: Hundreds of git mirrors and snapshots bought them time, but got harder to run as merges sped up.
assets/vo/s06-2bed6079.mp3: Then they noticed: almost every user was an agent or an automated job, always online.
assets/vo/s06-a7598350.mp3: So why give each one a full copy?
assets/vo/s07-e2297691.mp3: So they built Scion, their own version control system.
assets/vo/s07-aed5f8de.mp3: The server holds the code and does the heavy work: history, commits, merges.
assets/vo/s07-092140e0.mp3: Each client keeps a small cache, a local copy of what it already fetched, and asks the server for the rest.
assets/vo/s08-f637203c.mp3: Every change is saved as a changeset: just the files that changed, with links to their contents.
assets/vo/s08-1090bc48.mp3: Each link is made from the content itself, so the data never changes and any cache can keep it.
assets/vo/s09-0aeb06af.mp3: A client asks only for the folders it needs, starting from the top.
assets/vo/s09-a225c073.mp3: Some files arrive only when a program reads them.
assets/vo/s10-e6ca2860.mp3: When a job needs data, it looks nearest first.
assets/vo/s10-04d78c60.mp3: First, scion-daemon: a cache on its own machine, shared by every job running there.
assets/vo/s10-c1ff6599.mp3: Next, scion-cache: servers in the same region that keep data ready in memory.
assets/vo/s10-db2f680a.mp3: Last, the main scion servers: the source of truth, reading from the database and cloud storage.
assets/vo/s10-baba66a0.mp3: Each layer answers over 99 percent of requests itself.
assets/vo/s11-8b0a73cc.mp3: It needs 200 times less computing than their old git mirrors,
assets/vo/s11-879365d8.mp3: and checkouts take seconds, not minutes.
assets/vo/s12-73070eeb.mp3: Many jobs never copy the code. They just ask the server, like: what changed in this commit?
assets/vo/s12-e3017587.mp3: Tools that find and undo bad changes work the same way.
assets/vo/s13-2987d2c6.mp3: With so many changes, making each one wait its turn doesn't work.
assets/vo/s13-05c56077.mp3: So changes land first, and tests run after.
assets/vo/s13-dae19309.mp3: If two clash, Claude usually fixes it before a human would notice.
assets/vo/s14-947dc075.mp3: The catch: a Scion client can't do much without the server.
assets/vo/s14-03eefa85.mp3: Branches are discouraged, and code review, search and testing had to be rebuilt.
assets/vo/s14-7f3367f9.mp3: In return: far less data per copy, and a system that grows by adding machines.
assets/vo/s15-139085d6.mp3: So Anthropic says Scion isn't for most teams, only for giant codebases with swarms of agents.
assets/vo/s15-56c13c43.mp3: Instead, they're sharing ideas that git could borrow.
assets/vo/s16-b0281086.mp3: Seven people built it in five months, with Claude.
assets/vo/s17-68a3d23e.mp3: Git copies everything. Scion asks only for what it needs. Follow for more AI basics.
